questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Surfing and meeting new people.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The surfing community on campus is very cool and welcoming. The people taught me to surf. We even planned surf trips up and down the coast (even going to Mexico).

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival the campus was very organized for incoming students. Even applying for courses was easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They have a student service for exchange students that helped us. They even offered free SIM cards and a good discount on a cheap monthly plan.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in I-house but I believe you can apply for all housing accommodations if you want to. I-house is a great initiative that houses 50% locals and 50% foreigners (full time students and exchange). Pretty cool but quite expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We shared a kitchen between four people in our "suite"/appartment on campus. The campus offered a variety of different meal plans and unfortunately it was mandatory to get one when you live on campus. Luckily you can pick the cheapest one to buy coffee and snacks.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's expensive as hell!!! But you easily make friends and it is super convenient for classes as well especially in the US where no public transport exist. Very good vibes though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Pretty cool they had an add-and-drop period going into the semester where you could go to a couple of extra courses to see if you found them interesting and a couple of weeks in you could drop those you did not want to attend.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It was a pretty simple process. If you had trouble you could contact the administration but also go directly to the professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I think I got all but one course.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to have some electives as it makes it easier and you are able to pick some fun courses and try to find some friends you can register with.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was alright.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Around the same academic level as in Copenhagen (maybe even a bit lower) but with an insane inflation in the grades. People were sad with getting a B.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: They implemented and stuck to streaming and recording the lectures. Way better! The students also had more influence on the lectures and syllabus.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 2 semesters

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Game Theory
Economic Development
Economics of the Environment

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
questions.answer:
Prog Computational Social Sci
Economics of Ocean Resources 
Topics in Macroeconomics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them but the game theory was really good

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had everything!!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had literally everything.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the surf club. Highly recommended.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Drive up and down the coast. Go to Mexico and eat tacos, Drive up the coast on highway 101 and see the small surf villages of Encinitas etc. We also did road trips to Grand Canyon and Yosemite.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was okay but the food was a big change.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the social and athletic clubs and just speak to people in your classes and where you live.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Transportation and food.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Surfing and welcoming.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Appreciate the ocean, the weather and don't be afraid to say yes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go surfing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The surfing and the people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The money

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
